characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: D/Max-2200, Cu target, operated at 40 kV and 40 mA, scan rate 4° per min
characterization_methods.key_findings: As-cast 3Cr strip composed of austenite (γ) + ferrite (δ), austenite major matrix; austenite lattice constant 3.56 Å for 3Cr.
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify constituent phases and determine austenite lattice constant (JADE)

characterization_methods.key_findings: Ferrite uniformly distributed in austenite matrix; 3Cr strip shows enlarged, partly block-like, dendritic-outlined ferrite particles aligned in rows.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: polished metallographic sections, 20 µm scale bar

characterization_methods.key_findings: Dense tangled dislocation network in austenite of 3Cr (more than 0Cr); very weak κ-carbide superlattice; ferrite shows no superlattice/secondary phases.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: BF/DF imaging with selected-area diffraction patterns, 500 nm scale bars
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine dislocations and carbide precipitation in austenite and ferrite

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: MTS Criterion Model 44 mechanical property tester, 10 kN capacity
characterization_methods.key_findings: As-cast 3Cr: YS 617±4 MPa, UTS 896±28 MPa, TE 33.2±7%; 3Cr average strain hardening rate 2048 MPa.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: gauge size 20 mm × 4 mm × 1 mm, strain rate 1×10^-3 s^-1, room temperature (not explicitly stated), averaged over 3 measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure yield strength, ultimate tensile strength and total elongation

characterization_methods.key_findings: Measured 3Cr composition: Mn 27.6, Al 8.4, C 1.3, Cr 2.8 wt.%, Fe balance.
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine actual chemical composition of the strips

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SJ-600G Electronic Water Displacement Density Analyzer
characterization_methods.key_findings: Measured average density of the 3Cr strip is 6.45 g/cm3.
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure average density of the strips

analytical_models.equation_role: Estimates the maximum cooling rate during near-rapid solidification

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Liquid metal poured into a copper mold at a rotating speed of 600 r/min
computational_details.simulation_method: calculated maximum cooling rate of the near-rapid solidification process

analytical_models.equation_role: Determines austenite lattice constant from XRD peak positions

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: XRD patterns of the as-cast strips
computational_details.simulation_method: XRD profile analysis / lattice parameter refinement
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Lattice constants derived from the measured XRD patterns

defect_interactions.interaction_type: dislocation propagation blocked by phase interfaces
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Increase of δ-ferrite fraction in Cr-containing strips can block dislocation propagation due to more phase-interface areas, which may decrease plasticity.

interfaces.interface_notes: No numerical interface characterisation (coherency, boundary type) specific to the as-cast 3Cr strip is reported; C23C6 grain-boundary carbides form only in 9Cr.
interfaces.phase_evolution: FA solidification mode: L (liquid) → L+δ (high temperature ferrite) → L+δ+γ (austenite) → δ+γ.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: With Cr addition the as-cast 3Cr strip shows lower yield strength (617±4 MPa vs 724±16 MPa for as-cast 0Cr, ~ -15%) and lower total elongation (33.2±7% vs 40.8±8%) but a higher steady-stage strain hardening rate (2048 MPa vs 1626 MPa for 0Cr).

processing_steps.method: induction melting of a high-purity elemental charge
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingot made from high purity Fe (99.99%), Mn (99.9%), Al (99.9%), C (99.8%) and Cr (99.9%); the alloy ingot was reheated to melt by an induction coil.

processing_steps.method: centrifugal casting into a copper mold
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Liquid metal poured into a copper mold at a rotating speed of 600 r/min; obtained strip size (60–80) mm × 60 mm × 2.5 mm. No post-solidification heat treatment (as-cast terminal state).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: averaged over 3 measurements (more than three tensile specimens per test)

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain and true stress-strain / strain-hardening-rate curves of as-cast 3Cr strip (Fig. 3a, b); 3Cr engineering curve ends near 40% strain with UTS below 1000 MPa, and strain-hardening-rate plateau increases with Cr content.

precipitates.distribution: Very weak κ-carbide superlattice in the austenite SADP; sizes too small to identify by TEM (Cr addition suppresses κ-carbide precipitation relative to 0Cr).

phases_present.morphology: partly block-like particles with dendritic outlines, larger and more abundant than in 0Cr, locally aligned in rows

precipitates.distribution: DF/SADP of 3Cr ferrite show no superlattice; almost clean features without evident secondary phases (DO3 only appears in 6Cr and 9Cr).

microstructure_list.region: dispersed second-phase particles in the austenite matrix (located at centers of austenite grains)

structures.overall_structure: Two-phase γ + δ microstructure: austenite (γ, fcc) is the major matrix phase with δ-ferrite second-phase particles uniformly distributed in the austenite matrix. δ-ferrite first nucleated and grew from the melt following the FA solidification mode L → L+δ → L+δ+γ → δ+γ.

unmapped_findings: The as-cast 3Cr strip was produced under the same solidification condition, so its residual stress caused by rapid cooling is similar to the other strips; reduction of nano-scale κ-carbides increases the formation ability of dislocations, giving 3Cr (and 6Cr) a higher dislocation density than the Cr-free strip.

Compared with as-cast strips, the strain hardening rate of annealed strips except 9Cr clearly decreases; the reduction in strain hardening rate of the annealed 3Cr strip is the largest, about 500 MPa (relevant to the annealed condition of the same alloy, not the as-cast state of this sample).

Cr addition in Fe–28Mn–9Al-1.2C strips is reported to expand the solid solubility of Al and C and reduce the driving force for κ-carbide formation, so higher Cr content gives less κ-carbide precipitation and increases dislocation density in the austenite matrix.
κ-carbides in the as-cast 0Cr strip have an average diameter of 8 nm (given for reference when comparing Cr-containing strips).
